title: Emrys and the Escarpment
premise: Wren Sandoval, a disgraced mountain guide, is hired by old rival Cass Merrow to lead an illegal winter traverse of the Escarpment before its concession permits expire and the route is sealed forever. The crew discovers a derelict survey station holding records that prove Wren's blacklisting was engineered to bury a fatal expedition a decade ago—one Cass's family helped cover up. As permits lapse and a corporate recovery team closes in, Wren must choose between exposing the truth and keeping the crew alive. In the end, Wren brings everyone home, releases the records anonymously, and finally belongs somewhere: among the people who walked out with them.
about_author: Mara Ashgrove is a former backcountry ranger who writes adventure fiction from a cabin she refuses to geotag. Her novels are known for terrain so vivid readers check their own bootlaces.

chapters.title: The Blacklist
chapters.summary: Wren Sandoval's POV. Working a low-stakes trail job under a false name, Wren gets word their last client has reported them—again. The chapter establishes Wren's exile, meticulous competence, and the rule they live by: stay invisible. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking old grief.

chapters.title: An Offer from Cass Merrow
chapters.summary: Cass arrives unannounced with a contract: guide a five-person crew across the Escarpment in eleven days, before concession permits expire and the range closes to civilians. Wren refuses; Cass mentions a name from the past—the Kestrel Expedition. POV: Wren. Beat: dread rekindled into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: Wren interviews the team Cass has gathered: medic Odile, geologist Tomas, radio tech Priya, and Cass herself. Each has a reason to be unfindable. Wren realizes this crew was assembled for deniability, not skill alone. POV: Wren. Beat: unease sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Was Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Wren's voice: ten years ago, the Kestrel Expedition lost two climbers above the escarpment wall, and Wren took the blame. The memory of the storm and the broken radio. Beat: guilt as a physical scar; the reader learns why the route was forbidden.

chapters.title: Permits and Deadlines
chapters.summary: Priya decodes the legal fine print: once the concessions lapse, the Escarpment becomes corporate extraction land, and anything found inside stays sealed. Cass insists the traverse is about mapping what will be lost. Wren suspects otherwise. POV: Priya. Beat: suspicion braided with idealism.

chapters.title: The Threshold
chapters.summary: Day one on the mountain. Weather window holds; the crew crosses the boundary marker where Wren was banned. Small tensions surface—Tomas hoards data, Cass gives orders like she owns the ridge. POV: Wren. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by trespass.

chapters.title: First Fall
chapters.summary: A cornice collapse nearly takes Odile into a crevasse; Wren's rescue is flawless but costs them a day. That night Cass admits she knew the route was rated beyond the season. POV: Odile. Beat: trust earned through crisis, doubt planted by confession.

chapters.title: The Station on the Shoulder
chapters.summary: The crew finds a derelict survey station—Kestrel-era equipment, still powered by a geothermal tap nobody mapped. Inside: sealed logbooks. Tomas wants them; Wren orders them left. POV: Tomas. Beat: temptation versus loyalty.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: A three-day storm pins the crew in tents. Rations tighten; tempers fray. Priya's radio catches a garbled transmission—a recovery team is inbound behind them. POV: Priya. Beat: claustrophobia and the first open accusation between Wren and Cass.

chapters.title: Cass's Version
chapters.summary: Trapped by weather, Cass tells her side of Kestrel: her father led it, the deaths were covered up to protect the concession, and Wren was the convenient scapegoat. She hired Wren to find proof. POV: Cass. Beat: sympathy for an unreliable narrator.

chapters.title: The Logbooks
chapters.summary: Tomas, unable to resist, has already opened the logbooks. They contain Kestrel's real findings: a mineral strike worth billions—and evidence the 'accident' was a deliberate cutoff of the retreat line. POV: Tomas. Beat: horror at knowledge that can't be unread.

chapters.title: Divided Camp
chapters.summary: The crew splits: sell the data, publish it, or burn it and walk away. Wren, confronted with proof of their own innocence, must decide whether vindication is worth the danger. POV: Wren. Beat: the theme of power's corruption made personal.

chapters.title: The Recovery Team
chapters.summary: The corporate team makes contact—polite, armed, offering extraction and silence in exchange for the logs. Their leader knows Wren by name and reputation. POV: Odile. Beat: menace wrapped in courtesy; the stakes turn lethal.

chapters.title: Running the Icefield
chapters.summary: Wren leads the crew off-trail across unmapped ice to evade pursuit, using decade-old memories of Kestrel's route. A near-miss with a hidden moulin. POV: Wren. Beat: mastery and terror fused; Wren becomes the guide they were meant to be.

chapters.title: Betrayal at High Camp
chapters.summary: Someone signaled the recovery team. Evidence points to Tomas, but the truth is worse: Cass cut a deal to protect her family's name, planning to hand over everything but Wren. POV: Cass. Beat: betrayal that hurts because it's half-understandable.

chapters.title: The Wall
chapters.summary: The only way out is the escarpment face where Kestrel died—in worsening weather, pursued. Wren lays out the climb honestly: some may not make it. Each chooses. POV: Wren. Beat: grim communion; belonging forged in shared risk.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Mid-ascent, the recovery team's helicopter goes down in the pass behind them; the pursuers become survivors needing rescue. Wren turns the climb around. POV: Odile. Beat: the moral climax—mercy over vengeance, at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Kestrel Col
chapters.summary: At the col, Wren finds the final Kestrel cache: the original radio, never broken—deliberately silenced. Full truth lands. Cass breaks. POV: Wren. Beat: grief transmuted into clarity; memory honored at last.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: The descent through the storm, hauling injured strangers alongside crew. Cass surrenders the logs to Wren without conditions. One climber is lost—not to the mountain, but choosing to stay with the wreck site until relief comes. POV: Priya. Beat: sorrow and solidarity entwined.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: They cross out of the concession hours after it lapses—no longer trespassers, no longer protected, no longer hunted. The recovery team's survivors corroborate everything. POV: Wren. Beat: exhaustion edged with improbable freedom.

chapters.title: The Release
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the Kestrel records surface publicly via anonymous channels; concessions are revoked pending inquiry. Wren declines credit, declines Cass's offer to rebuild a guiding company together—for now. POV: Wren. Beat: quiet justice; power refused.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Spring. Wren guides a small, honest trip on open ground with Odile and Priya beside them. The wilderness forgives nothing—but Wren no longer needs forgiveness, only company. Final beat: belonging found not in a place cleared of the past, but in people who carry it with you.
